title: no-halt-agent Sprint 2: pipe モード + claude-agent ロスレス生存 [MILESTONE]

planning_decisions.decision: Story granularity kept as-is (3 stories, no split).
planning_decisions.rationale: The three stories are cleanly layered and non-overlapping in BEHAVIOR: (1) spike = measure real-claude control_request deadline (gating), (2) mechanism = pipe-mode ptyhost + generic offset-ack line replay + persistence + overflow detection (fake-emitter verifiable, no claude), (3) adoption = claudeagent.Client thin-client + permstate/transcript reconstruction + real-claude E2E. No story bundles independent behaviors that warrant a split. The task's suggested breakdown matches the natural mechanism-vs-consumer seam.

Story 1 is a gating spike whose result can trigger an ADR-0004 revisit — it MUST complete and PASS before any mechanism is built. Story 2 and Story 3 both extend the pipe-mode ptyhost AND share internal/tab/claudeagent files (Story 2 lands the generic replay client + offset store there; Story 3 rewrites client.go/manager.go + adds discover.go in the same package). Overlapping file-touch + the mechanism→consumer dependency make parallelism unsafe.

planning_decisions.decision: Reuse the S3f2658 ptyhost wire almost entirely; the ONLY sanctioned protocol growth is a stderr-delivery frame (or 1-byte stream discriminator) for pipe mode.
planning_decisions.rationale: priority_rule 6 + ADR-0002 (frozen-minimal protocol). The Ring is already absolute-offset; MsgAck/MsgAttach/MsgData/MsgStatus already exist and Ring.readFromLocked already returns the clamped start offset (which IS the overflow-detection primitive). So pipe mode needs only: mode-aware spawn (pipes vs PTY), a stdin-write path (reuse MsgInput), a no-op resize, and a way to deliver stderr separately from the NDJSON stdout stream. Adding one stderr frame is mandated by the design doc §6 ('stderr は別チャネル') and justified by ADR-0004, so it is not an ADR-0002 violation — but the implementer must keep it to the single minimal addition and record the exact wire choice in the run-phase decisions.

planning_decisions.decision: Overflow detection is palmux2-side via the clamped ATTACH start offset; ptyhost does NOT persist and does NOT auto-deny pending requests.
planning_decisions.rationale: ADR-0002 thin-holder + ADR-0004. The ptyhost holds the ring and echoes the clamped start offset it already computes; palmux2 compares requested-last-ack vs returned-start and, if start > requested, declares 'lossless restore impossible → new session'. Persistence (sessions.json-equivalent last-ack) lives in palmux2 (Story 2 store). This keeps the surviving old-binary ptyhost claude-agnostic and the socket protocol frozen.

planning_decisions.decision: Replay reconstruction of transcript + permstate reuses the UNCHANGED processStreamMessage path — replayed NDJSON lines are fed back through the same parser.
planning_decisions.rationale: ADR-0004's core premise is that the stdout stream is the source of truth for transcript/permstate/MCP state. Therefore replaying last-ack+ lines through the existing normalize.go/permstate.go/transcript.go rebuilds state for free. normalize/permstate/transcript/mcp stay palmux2-side and unchanged (ADR-0002/0004), minimizing regression surface for AC-3-3.

planning_decisions.decision: The incus (in-container) agent path becomes an OPAQUE argv handed to a pipe-mode ptyhost, exactly as claudetui.spawnWithArgs does for the PTY path.
planning_decisions.rationale: Today claudeagent uses runtime.ExecCommander (incus exec, no -t, binary-clean) which returns an *exec.Cmd. For ptyhost the child must be an opaque argv/env/cwd. Convert via argv=[cmd.Path, cmd.Args[1:]...], env=cmd.Env, cwd=cmd.Dir — the identical technique S3f2658 used for the PTYCommander wrapper. ExecCommander's no-TTY binary-clean property is exactly what pipe mode needs.

spike.question: Does the claude CLI wait for (and accept) a response to an MCP-routed permission control_request LONGER than palmux2's realistic restart window (a few seconds to ~15s)? Or does it time out / cancel / abort the tool first?
spike.method: Go spike harness reusing claudeagent transport primitives (mirror ask_integration_test.go / bash_perm_integration_test.go real-claude wiring): spawn real claude in stream-json mode with an in-process MCP permission server, force a permission control_request, WITHHOLD the response for tiered delays (10s/30s/60s), then send allow and record whether the late response is accepted + the tool executes + the turn continues.
spike.gate: ADR-0004 revisit + HALT (escalate to user) IF the late allow is NOT accepted at ~15s (deadline shorter than restart window). PASS ⇒ proceed to Wave 2.

waves.rationale: Gating spike — REAL claude control_request deadline. Must PASS before building the replay mechanism it validates; a FAIL triggers an ADR-0004 revisit and halts the sprint (priority_rule 0).

Pipe-mode ptyhost + generic line-oriented offset-ack replay + persistence store + ring-overflow detection. Fully verifiable with a fake NDJSON emitter (no claude, no quota). Depends on the Wave-1 spike PASS.

claudeagent.Client thin-client migration onto the Wave-2 mechanism + permstate/transcript replay reconstruction + real-claude restart-crossing E2E. Depends on Wave 2 (mechanism) and shares claudeagent files with it, so it runs strictly after.

new_test_or_harness: internal/tab/claudeagent/spike_control_deadline_test.go (env-gated real-claude spike harness, mirroring ask_integration_test.go / bash_perm_integration_test.go) OR an equivalent throwaway harness under tests/
S862203-1.note: Pure spike — NO production code changes. Reuses existing claudeagent transport + MCP primitives at the library level to observe the exact production wire path.

production: internal/ptyhost/server.go (mode-aware spawn: pipes vs PTY; separate stdout+stderr read loops; MsgInput→stdin pipe; MsgResize no-op in pipe mode)
internal/ptyhost/protocol.go (HELLO.Mode/StatusFile.Mode = "pipe"; the single stderr-delivery frame/discriminator — the one sanctioned addition)
internal/ptyhost/ring.go (reuse as-is; instantiate a SECOND ring for stderr — likely no Ring code change)

internal/tab/claudeagent/ptyclient.go (NEW — generic line-oriented pipe-replay client: dial/HELLO/ATTACH-from-last-ack, NDJSON line reassembly across DATA boundaries, ACK-at-line-end, overflow detection)
internal/tab/claudeagent/offsetstore.go (NEW — sessions.json-equivalent last-ack offset persistence, atomic write; may extend existing store.go/sessions.go instead)
new_test: internal/ptyhost/pipe_test.go / server_test.go additions (pipe-mode spawn, stdout/stderr separation, kill-9 restart, overflow) with a FAKE NDJSON emitter child (testdata helper)
S862203-2.note: Touches internal/ptyhost AND internal/tab/claudeagent (the generic replay client + offset store land where Story 3 consumes them). This shared-package touch with Story 3 is the reason the two waves are serial.

production: internal/tab/claudeagent/client.go (LARGE — replace exec+StdinPipe/StdoutPipe/StderrPipe with pipe-mode ptyhost launch/attach; pumpStdout→Story-2 line replay client; pumpStderr→separate stderr channel; writeLine→INPUT frames; Close→SHUTDOWN/GC. Keep ALL argv/env assembly + control/MCP handling)

internal/tab/claudeagent/manager.go (EnsureClient launches via ptyhost; watchClient exit-detection via socket STATUS/disconnect; respawn = new pipe-mode ptyhost; --resume/invalid-resume/gate logic preserved)

internal/tab/claudeagent/discover.go (NEW — reconnect surviving agent ptyhosts on palmux2 startup + replay-driven permstate/transcript/pending-request reconstruction; mirror internal/tab/claudetui/discover.go DiscoverAndRestore)
internal/tab/claudeagent/provider.go (wire discovery + PalmuxBin/instancePrefix/RingSize plumbing, mirror claudetui provider)
cmd/palmux/main.go (invoke agent DiscoverAndRestore on startup, mirror the claudetui wiring)
unchanged: internal/tab/claudeagent/normalize.go, permstate.go, transcript.go, mcp.go, control.go, events.go, modes.go — stay palmux2-side; replay reconstruction reuses processStreamMessage (PD-5)
S862203-3.note: Highest-risk migration. Shares client.go/manager.go/store with Story 2 → serial.

real_claude_requirements.S862203-1: REQUIRED — the AC's whole purpose is real-claude control_request deadline behavior. Fake emitter cannot answer it. Runs on this box's real `claude`. Gates the sprint.
real_claude_requirements.S862203-2: NOT needed — fake NDJSON emitter (counter-tagged lines, controllable pace) as the ptyhost child makes ring/ACK/offset/replay/overflow + kill-9 restart deterministic and quota-free.
real_claude_requirements.S862203-3: AC-3-2 REQUIRED — real claude on `make serve INSTANCE=dev` (NEVER host palmux2): restart palmux2 mid-turn, prove (a) lossless transcript restore and (b) a restart-window permission request delivered→answered→tool executes. AC-3-1 wiring: fake emitter OK. AC-3-3: existing claudeagent unit + real-claude integration suite (ask/bash_perm/plan) regress cleanly.

forbidden_reminders: Do NOT restart/foreground the host palmux2 (it would kill the operator's live Claude session). All E2E/survival runs use `make serve INSTANCE=dev` (separate portman name + --tmux-prefix _pmx_dev_).
Ports via portman only; tmux via internal/tmux.Client only; no ~/.claude writes.

priority_rule 0: NEVER mark AC-S862203-1-1 or AC-S862203-3-2 as skipped/false-done. If a real-claude run is truly impossible under autopilot, escalate at the milestone review — do not fabricate a PASS.
adr_gate: If S862203-1 FAILS (claude aborts the control_request before ~15s), STOP: escalate an ADR-0004 revisit to the user (options per ADR notes: rely on claude to re-send the pending request on reconnect, or have ptyhost hold the request without auto-deny). Waves 2-3 assume the spike PASS.

run_decisions.decision: Harness reuses the real internal/tab/claudeagent.NewClient production wire path (--permission-prompt-tool mcp__palmux__permission_prompt, in-process mcpServer, mcp_message control_request/control_response) rather than a hand-rolled fake emitter, wrapped in a new env-gated test file internal/tab/claudeagent/spike_control_deadline_test.go (PALMUX_SPIKE_S862203_1=1, mirroring the existing PALMUX_SURVIVAL_SMOKE / PALMUX_REALINCUS_SMOKE gate pattern in internal/tab/claudetui). Zero production code changed.
run_decisions.rationale: The spike's entire purpose is measuring REAL claude CLI behaviour on the exact wire path production uses (priority_rule 0) -- a fake emitter cannot answer 'how long does claude wait for a control_request response'. Reusing NewClient/mcpServer verbatim (rather than reimplementing the MCP dispatch) guarantees the observed timing is production-representative.

run_decisions.decision: PermissionMode explicitly forced to "manual" in the harness's ClientOptions.
run_decisions.rationale: First run without this returned instantly with tool_executed=true but ZERO permission control_request ever observed -- this host's shared ~/.claude/settings.json (the ambient config for the very Claude Code session running this spike) sets permissions.defaultMode=bypassPermissions. NewClient always passes --setting-sources project,user, so that user-level default silently let the Bash tool run without ever invoking the permission_prompt MCP tool, defeating the spike. --permission-mode manual forces the CLI to ask every time regardless of the ambient settings.json, matching how the real Claude tab always requests permission (it never runs with bypassPermissions).

run_decisions.decision: Acceptance ('accepted') is judged by the ground-truth side effect (did the withheld Bash command actually write its marker file to disk) plus turn continuation (a `result` envelope arrives) and the ABSENCE of two negative signals: (a) a 'write control response' stdin-write-failure log (client.go logs this when the CLI process has already exited/closed stdin) and (b) the result envelope's own timestamp preceding the moment the late allow was actually sent (which would mean the turn ended before our response could possibly have reached the CLI).
run_decisions.rationale: The harness cannot see raw control_cancel_request frames on the wire -- client.go's pumpStdout silently drops that message type without forwarding it to onMessage, and this is production code the spike must not modify. The chosen signals (tool side-effect + turn-continuation + write-failure + timestamp-ordering) are the properties that actually matter for ADR-0004's replay design (did the late response get through and did the gated action actually happen), so the blind spot on raw cancel frames does not weaken the verdict.

run_decisions.decision: First implementation of the 'early result' check used a fixed racy time.After(delay+2s) window per tier and mislabelled the tier-10s run's legitimate POST-response completion as premature (observed_timeout_or_cancel=true even though accepted=true, tool_executed=true). Fixed by removing the window race entirely: the harness now blocks on a single unbounded (delay+90s ceiling) read of the result channel and compares the result envelope's OWN timestamp against the requester's recorded resolveAt timestamp after the fact, with a 50ms jitter margin.
run_decisions.rationale: A window sized off the expected delay will, by construction, sometimes still be open when the genuine post-response result naturally arrives a moment later -- racing a channel read against an estimated deadline is the wrong tool for distinguishing 'before' from 'after' when the actual timestamps are available and exact. Caught and fixed via a single-tier (10s) smoke run before spending quota on the full 3-tier run.

run_decisions.decision: restart_window_context in the result JSON is a REASONED ESTIMATE ("a few seconds to ~15s", sourced from ADR-0004/scenario-S862203-1.json's own framing plus prior sprints' timing data), not a freshly measured `make serve INSTANCE=dev` kill+respawn+reconnect cycle.
run_decisions.rationale: A fresh empirical measurement would require a full frontend+backend build cycle unrelated to the quota-sensitive real-claude question that actually gates the sprint (priority_rule: keep the harness to the minimum runs/cost needed). The 15s threshold used for the PASS/HALT gate is the one already load-bearing in ADR-0004 and the scenario doc, not a number this spike invented; a precise re-measurement is noted as cheap to obtain later if ever needed and does not change today's PASS verdict since all three tiers (10s/30s/60s) cleared it with wide margin.

run_decisions.decision: Result: PASS. All three tiers (10s, 30s, 60s) had accepted=true, tool_executed=true, turn_continued=true, observed_timeout_or_cancel=false, result_is_error=false. max_confirmed_delay_s=60. ADR-0004 gate CLEARS -- proceed to Wave 2 (S862203-2). No HALT, no escalation needed.
run_decisions.rationale: claude CLI 2.1.207 places no observable deadline on an outstanding mcp_message control_request within the tested range (up to 60s, 4x the ~15s restart-window threshold) -- it simply blocks the turn until the (in-process MCP) permission_prompt tool call resolves, then executes the now-allowed Bash command and completes the turn normally, exactly as ADR-0004 assumed but had left unverified. Full evidence in docs/sprint-logs/S862203/spike-S862203-1-1.json (raw_events per tier).

run_decisions.decision: The ONE sanctioned protocol growth (ADR-0004 §6 / PD-3) is a new MsgStderrData wire type, h→c only, payload-identical to MsgData (reuses EncodeData/DecodeData verbatim). There is no new client→server request to trigger it: the EXISTING MsgAttach handler, in ModePipe only, additionally (re)subscribes the connection to a second, symmetric ptyhost-side Ring (stderrRing) and writes its full retained content + live bytes over MsgStderrData as a side effect of the same ATTACH that establishes the stdout replay.
run_decisions.rationale: Keeps stdout on the EXISTING MsgData/ATTACH/ACK/STATUS path completely unchanged (S3f2658 wire reused verbatim) and avoids a second request/response pair (e.g. an ATTACH_STDERR) that would be a second protocol growth, not one. Reusing the Ring type for stderr (rather than inventing a stderr-specific structure) is itself further wire/logic reuse, not reinvention.

run_decisions.decision: ptyhost.Config gained Mode string ("" → defaults to ModePTY="pty"; ModePipe="pipe"), validated in NewServer (unknown mode is a construction error). spawn() branches into spawnPTY (unchanged creackpty.Start path, renamed) and spawnPipe (cmd.StdinPipe/StdoutPipe/StderrPipe, NO creackpty.Start — the same binary-clean technique S4d8b1c's runtime.ExecCommander already uses). MsgInput’s writeInput writes to the stdin pipe when set, else falls back to the PTY master (mutually exclusive by construction). MsgResize/resize() needed NO code change — it already no-ops on ptmx==nil, which is naturally true in pipe mode.
run_decisions.rationale: Config-level mode selection is the minimal, most reusable way to add a second holding strategy without duplicating the Server/handleConn/protocol-serving machinery (Run(), handleConn, STATUS, SHUTDOWN, orphan-GC discovery are all mode-agnostic and untouched). Discovering that RESIZE already no-ops for free (rather than needing an explicit mode branch) is itself evidence the existing code was already close to pipe-mode-ready.

run_decisions.decision: os/exec's documented invariant — “it is incorrect to call Wait before all reads from [StdoutPipe/StderrPipe] have completed” — is honored via a new stdioDone sync.WaitGroup: in ModePipe, waitChild() blocks on stdioDone.Wait() (satisfied once BOTH the stdout and stderr pump goroutines have independently observed EOF, which happens naturally once the child's own fds close on exit) before calling cmd.Wait(). ModePTY's waitChild() path is unchanged (ptmx is not exec.Cmd-owned, so no such ordering constraint applies there) except that the explicit ptmx.Close() is now gated to ModePTY only (ModePipe's pipes are auto-closed by cmd.Wait() itself; closing them again would double-close).
run_decisions.rationale: This ordering bug (calling Wait() concurrently with in-flight StdoutPipe/StderrPipe reads) is a real Go gotcha that silently truncates output under race — exactly the kind of loss AC-S862203-2-1/2-2 explicitly test for (integration tests reading full replayed content), so getting it wrong would have been a flaky, hard-to-diagnose failure rather than a clean one. Caught during implementation by reading the os/exec doc comments before wiring waitChild(), not by a failing test.

run_decisions.decision: internal/tab/claudeagent/ptyclient.go's PipeClient.Run(ctx, offset, onAttach) is a single blocking call (not split into a separate synchronous Attach() + Run()): it writes ATTACH once, then loops reading frames until the connection errors/closes/ctx is done. The overflow verdict (AttachResult) is reported via a one-shot onAttach callback invoked synchronously from inside that same loop on the FIRST MsgData frame, before any of that frame's bytes are dispatched to onLine — so a caller wanting to bail out on overflow observes the verdict before any (potentially gapped) line is processed.
run_decisions.rationale: A two-phase Attach()-then-Run() API would need to hand off already-buffered-but-unread frame state between the two calls (the ATTACH reply's own DATA frame has to be fed into the SAME line-reassembly buffer subsequent live DATA frames use), which is exactly the kind of internal-state seam that invites bugs; collapsing to one blocking Run() loop that reports its one interesting intermediate result via callback removes that seam entirely while still giving the caller everything AC-S862203-2-3 needs (inspect Overflowed before deciding whether to keep consuming lines).

run_decisions.decision: LineHandler's contract is: return nil → PipeClient.Run() sends an informational MsgAck for that line's end offset and continues; return a non-nil error → Run() stops immediately WITHOUT acking/persisting that line, propagating the error to the caller. This single contract IS the kill-9 simulation primitive used by TestPipeClient_Kill9Reconnect_RedeliversUnackedLine_ExactlyOnce (the test's LineHandler deliberately returns an error instead of calling OffsetStore.Save for one line, then asserts the reconnect redelivers exactly that line first) — no separate/parallel “kill” code path was needed in PipeClient itself.
run_decisions.rationale: A generic “line processing failed, don't advance” contract naturally IS what a kill -9 looks like from the replay mechanism's point of view (some in-memory work happened, nothing was durably recorded) — building the test on top of the real contract (rather than a special test-only hook) means the test also validates the contract Story 3 will actually rely on when processStreamMessage errors mid-line.

run_decisions.decision: OffsetStore (internal/tab/claudeagent/offsetstore.go) is a NEW, separate on-disk file (agent_offsets.json) rather than a field added to sessions.json's existing PersistedShape, but reuses sessions.json's exact persistence mechanics (atomic write-then-rename, 0o600, same package-private tabKey/CanonicaliseTabID helper via a thin offsetKey wrapper) and Store's file-per-concern layout convention.
run_decisions.rationale: Task step 2 said 'Reuse claudeagent's existing Store/sessions.json layout style' — interpreted as reusing the STYLE (atomic write, tab-key shape) rather than the SAME FILE, because offset acks are written far more frequently (potentially every processed NDJSON line) than session bookkeeping; sharing one file would mean every ack write also serializes/rewrites the full sessions map, and a rare torn-write bug in one concern could take the other down with it. Reusing tabKey (rather than reimplementing key canonicalisation) keeps the two stores from ever disagreeing about tab identity.

run_decisions.decision: Tests use a new fake NDJSON emitter, internal/ptyhost/testdata/fake_ndjson.go (env-driven: FAKE_NDJSON_COUNT/START/DELAY_MS/STDERR_COUNT/EXIT_AFTER), reused by internal/tab/claudeagent's tests via a relative-path `go build` of the SAME file (not duplicated) — mirroring how internal/ptyhost/testdata/fake_child.go is compiled by internal/ptyhost's own tests. claudeagent's tests spin up a REAL ptyhost.Server in-process (goroutine, mirroring claudetui's inProcessLaunchPtyHost pattern) rather than a mock/stub server, so PipeClient is exercised against the genuine wire protocol end-to-end. No real claude process and no quota is used anywhere in this story's tests, per the scenario's real_claude:"NOT needed" gate.
run_decisions.rationale: Reusing one fake-emitter source file (rather than a claudeagent-local copy) keeps the two packages' tests asserting against the identical child behavior, so a future change to the emitter's shape doesn't silently diverge between the ptyhost-level and claudeagent-level test suites. Driving a REAL ptyhost.Server (not a hand-rolled protocol mock) means the tests validate PipeClient against the actual frame encoding/Ring/subscription code paths Story 3 will run in production, not against a re-implementation of them that could drift from the real thing.

run_decisions.decision: Result: COMPLETE. internal/ptyhost gained ModePipe spawn (spawnPipe, stdin/stdout/stderr pipes, no PTY) + a second stderrRing + the MsgStderrData wire addition + HELLO/StatusFile.Mode reflecting the real mode + a --mode flag on `palmux ptyhost`. internal/tab/claudeagent gained the generic PipeClient (line-reassembly-across-frames, ACK, overflow detection) and OffsetStore (atomic per-tab last-ack persistence), fully covered by fake-emitter tests at both layers: internal/ptyhost/pipe_test.go (8 tests: HELLO mode, stdout/stderr separation, stdin-pipe INPUT, RESIZE no-op, ACK no-op, kill-9 reconnect no-dup/no-loss, overflow detection, negative control) and internal/tab/claudeagent/{ptyclient_test.go,offsetstore_test.go} (10 tests: line reassembly, clean reconnect resume, kill-9 unacked-line-redelivered-exactly-once, overflow surfaced as AttachResult.Overflowed, negative control, OffsetStore round-trip/atomicity/clear/key-scoping). `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` clean; targeted suites + full `go test ./...` (28 packages) all green, 3x repeat runs of the new suites showed no flakiness. No production code outside internal/ptyhost and internal/tab/claudeagent (2 new files only, no existing claudeagent file touched) was modified — client.go/manager.go/discover.go wiring is explicitly Story 3's serial follow-on per PD-2/PD-6.
run_decisions.rationale: Matches the story's scope exactly: mechanism only (ptyhost pipe mode + generic replay client + persistence + overflow detection), fully fake-emitter-verifiable, zero real-claude/quota usage, zero protocol growth beyond the single ADR-0004-§6-sanctioned stderr frame, zero ADR-0002 violations (ptyhost remains claude-agnostic and non-persisting throughout).
